A.explanation: 0 V would mean all 12 V is lost inside the battery, but the lost volts $Ir$ is only $8 \text{ V}$, not $12 \text{ V}$.

B.explanation: Terminal p.d. is $V = E - Ir = 12 - 8 = 4 \text{ V}$.

C.explanation: 8 V is the p.d. lost across the $0.05 \text{ }\Omega$ internal resistance ($160 \times 0.05$), not the terminal p.d. remaining for the motor.

D.explanation: 12 V is the e.m.f. on open circuit; with 160 A flowing, internal resistance causes a drop so terminal p.d. is lower.

hints: Notice the battery is modelled as 12 V e.m.f. in series with 0.05 ohm internal resistance, both carrying the 160 A motor current.
Recall that terminal p.d. is the e.m.f. minus the volts lost inside the battery, given by $V = E - Ir$.
Calculate the lost volts $Ir = 160 \text{ A} \times 0.05 \text{ }\Omega$ first, then subtract that value from 12 V.
walkthrough: Identify the useful data from the diagram: e.m.f. $E = 12 \text{ V}$, internal resistance $r = 0.05 \text{ }\Omega$, and current $I = 160 \text{ A}$ through the battery and motor in series.
State the governing rule for a source delivering current: terminal p.d. $V = E - Ir$, where $Ir$ is the p.d. lost across the internal resistance.
Substitute values with units to find the lost volts: $Ir = 160 \text{ A} \times 0.05 \text{ }\Omega = 8.0 \text{ V}$.
Subtract from the e.m.f. to find what remains across the terminals: $V = 12 \text{ V} - 8.0 \text{ V} = 4 \text{ V}$, with a unit check giving volts.
